title: AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY SEEDS AND FARMERS' SELF-RELIANCE THROUGH BBSSL
body_text:
Ministry of Cooperation has set up Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 to act as an apex organization for production, procurement, processing, branding, labelling, packaging, storage, marketing, distribution and strategic research & development of quality seeds with a clear vision to build a strong, farmer-centric seed system through a cooperative-led structure.
Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) has so far introduced seeds of 18 crops and 124 varieties in the market under the 'Bharat Beej' brand for distribution across the country. Further, BBSSL has undertaken initiatives for developing production and quality-testing requirements for vegetable seeds in accordance with the prescribed seed quality and regulatory standards.
During the financial year 2025–26, BBSSL produced 75,535 metric tonnes of seeds through its associated seed-producing farmers under the seed production programme for the 'Bharat Beej' brand. The programme facilitates farmers' participation in organised seed production and provides technical support for the production of seeds in accordance with the prescribed quality and certification standards.
For the conservation of traditional indigenous varieties, BBSSL has initiated a programme in Uttarakhand focusing on the identification, conservation, multiplication and documentation of such varieties. BBSSL's activities include the expansion of domestic seed production, conservation of indigenous genetic resources, and distribution of quality seeds through the cooperative network, thereby contributing to the objective of reducing the country's dependence on imported seeds and strengthening self-reliance in the seed sector.
This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Cooperation informed the Rajya Sabha that Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL), an apex cooperative body set up under the MSCS Act 2002, has introduced 124 varieties of seeds across 18 crops under the 'Bharat Beej' brand. In FY 2025-26, BBSSL produced 75,535 metric tonnes of seeds through associated farmers, and it has also launched a conservation programme for traditional indigenous seed varieties in Uttarakhand. The initiative aims to expand domestic seed production, conserve genetic resources, and reduce India's dependence on imported seeds.
enrichment.context:
BBSSL was registered in 2023 alongside two other national-level cooperatives (for exports and organic products) as part of the government's push to revitalize the cooperative sector through the 'Sahakar se Samriddhi' vision under the newly created Ministry of Cooperation (established 2021). The seed cooperative model seeks to integrate small and marginal farmers into organised seed production chains, ensuring quality control, certification, and fair returns, while reducing reliance on private or imported seed sources—an issue of strategic importance given India's historical dependence on imported hybrid seeds for certain crops like vegetables and oilseeds.

The conservation of indigenous seed varieties, such as the Uttarakhand initiative, ties into India's broader agrobiodiversity conservation efforts under the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights (PPVFR) Act, 2001, and global commitments like the Nagoya Protocol on access and benefit-sharing of genetic resources. Strengthening farmer-owned cooperative seed systems is also seen as a way to enhance agricultural resilience, reduce input costs, and support the government's self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) agenda in the farm sector.

prelims_questions.question: Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL), mentioned frequently in news, was established under which legislation?
prelims_questions.explanation: BBSSL is registered as an apex cooperative organisation under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002, to handle production, processing, and marketing of quality seeds.

prelims_questions.question: Under which brand name has BBSSL introduced seeds of 124 varieties across 18 crops?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states BBSSL has introduced these seed varieties under the 'Bharat Beej' brand for nationwide distribution.
